cf.title: Implement missing join selectivity estimation for range types
cf.authors: Haibo Yan (billyean), Maxime Schoemans (mschoema), Mahmoud SAKR (mahmsakr), Diogo Repas (diogo.repas), Zhicheng Luo (zcsysu.163.com)

input.subject: Implement missing join selectivity estimation for range types

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal or the design of the estimator. demand-1 shows the thread has no user report, but the cost falls only on queries that join on range columns, so it is a request for evidence. maintenance-fit-2 is decisive: no committer has reviewed the v5 to v9 rework, and the January 2024 ASan crash is not shown to be gone.

brief.title: Join selectivity estimation for range and multirange operators
brief.problem: For joins on range columns such as t1.r << t2.r, the planner uses a fixed default selectivity of 0.005 and ignores the bounds histograms that ANALYZE already collects. Bad estimates can lead to poor join order and join methods in queries that join on range columns.
brief.proposed_design: rangejoinsel uses the lower and upper bounds histograms of both sides, merged in one walk, to estimate <<, >> and && (v5 onward drops &<, &>, @>, <@). A second patch applies the same outer-bounds estimator to multirange and mixed range/multirange joins. A third patch moves the helper functions duplicated in the two selfuncs files into a backend-private rangetypes_selfuncs.h.
user_visible_surface: New join selectivity functions for range operators <<, >>, && in pg_proc.dat, set as oprjoin in pg_operator.dat.
Same for multirange and mixed range/multirange operators <<, >>, &&.
Changed row estimates and plans for range and multirange joins.
Estimators fall back to the default selectivity when the comparator or subtype_diff function fails statistic_proc_security_check().
author_claims: Estimation error is about 0.5% for the covered operators, based on the authors' experiments.
The paper's algorithm beats the estimators in Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL and Postgres.
Estimates stay accurate on data with many duplicate ranges, even without MCV statistics for ranges.
For multiranges, && can overestimate on sparse values, but this matches existing restriction selectivity and beats the fixed default.
v9 passes the full regression suite, and new privileges.sql tests fail without the security checks.
brief.thread_state: After a 2023 review by Tomas Vondra, Tom Lane and others, Haibo Yan revived the patch in 2026 and reviewed v6 to v8 with Maxime Schoemans. Bryan Green found a missing statistic_proc_security_check(), fixed in v9, and no committer has replied since; CFbot reports the patch needs a rebase.
unclear: The material has no measurements for v9 scoped to <<, >> and &&, only for v1 and the paper.
The thread does not show planning-time cost of the merge walk at high statistics targets.
The thread does not settle the CFbot ASan crash in calc_hist_join_selectivity reported in January 2024.
No plan or timeline is given for the scalar inequality join case that Tomas Vondra and Tom Lane said matters more.
The material does not say whether new pg_proc entries need a catversion bump or have upgrade effects.

objections.title: No user report shows range or multirange joins being misestimated
objections.failure_scenario: A committer takes on a new histogram merge-walk estimator for range and multirange joins, plus a new privilege-check path, and owns its bugs and plan changes. If few production queries join on <<, >> or && between range columns, the plan gains reach few users while the ASan history and security surface stay with the project.
objections.argument: The patch began as a course project (message #7), and Tomas Vondra said he did not remember ever seeing an inequality join on a range column (message #6). The demand signals are reviewers calling it useful (message #15) and synthetic tables built to show the effect (messages #7, #20). No -general or -bugs report, production plan or user workload appears in the thread. Tom Lane's point (message #13) that scalar priority is no reason to reject is a different question from whether range joins have users.
objections.author_must_show: Which real workloads, such as temporal or scheduling schemas, join on range <<, >> or && today, and what bad plans do they get from the 0.005 default?

critic.reasoning: The thread has no user report or production plan, and message #6 says range joins are rare. The cost falls only on queries that join on range columns, so this supports asking for demand evidence and does not support a rejection.

objections.title: No committer has engaged with the 2026 series
objections.failure_scenario: A committer pushes v9 late in a cycle. A buildfarm member later reproduces the ASan out-of-bounds read reported in messages #16 and #18, or a user reports a plan regression on range joins. The committer must then fix an estimator that no other committer has reviewed since 2023.
objections.argument: The 2023 committer comments (messages #2-#6, #13) were about v1-v3. The v5-v9 rework was reviewed only by co-authors and non-committers (messages #21-#32), and message #28 says a committer is still needed. The original code came from a course project (message #7), and message #17 says the author could not confirm the CFbot crash was fixed. The CF entry has crossed three CommitFests and now needs a rebase.
objections.author_must_show: Has a committer familiar with selfuncs reviewed the v9 design, and is the 2024 ASan failure shown to be gone on CFbot?

critic.reasoning: The thread shows no committer reply after message #13, and the v5 to v9 rework had a security gap found only in September 2026. This belongs in the committability field and must not raise the verdict on the design.

refuted.title: Merge-walk estimator is tied to range types, not shaped for scalar reuse
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds the paper's estimator for scalar inequality joins in selfuncs.c and writes its own histogram merge walk. A bug later found in one copy, such as the halving error fixed in message #9, gets fixed there only. The other estimator keeps the wrong result until someone compares their plans.
refuted.argument: Tomas Vondra (message #6) and Tom Lane (message #13) call the scalar case the more important one, and the authors say the same algorithm applies there (messages #1, #4). Message #7 plans the scalar work as a separate patch in different files with "slight differences". Patch 3 puts the shared helpers in a header private to the range-family selfuncs, so a scalar implementation cannot reuse the walk. Tom's objection to duplicated functions in message #13 would then apply across three files instead of two.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the merge walk over two bounds histograms be written as a type-agnostic routine that a later scalar inequality estimator would call, and not copy?

critic.reasoning: The failure needs a scalar patch that does not exist yet, and that patch could move the walk to a shared place. Postgres already keeps range histogram code apart from scalar code, because range bounds use RangeBound comparison and scalars also need MCV handling (messages #4, #7).

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The patch adds join selectivity functions to pg_proc.dat and sets them as oprjoin in pg_operator.dat.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: Row estimates and plans change for joins on range and multirange <<, >> and &&.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The estimators run comparator and subtype_diff functions over statistics, guarded by statistic_proc_security_check() since v9.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Two new histogram-based join estimators and a shared private header stay in the planner's selectivity code.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The merge walk runs at plan time for range join clauses; its cost at high statistics targets is not shown.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is the ASan out-of-bounds read in calc_hist_join_selectivity, reported in messages #16 and #18, shown to be gone in v9 on CFbot?
Which real workloads join on range <<, >> or && today, and what bad plans do they get from the 0.005 default?
What is the estimation error of v9 for <<, >> and && only, including data with many duplicate ranges?
How much planning time does the merge walk add for a range join at a statistics target of 10000?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the selectivity estimation code in selfuncs. Tomas Vondra and Tom Lane commented on v1 to v3 in 2023, and no committer has replied on v5 to v9.
committability.liability: The owner signs for plan changes on range and multirange joins, the correctness of the histogram merge walk, and the privilege check path, for as long as the estimators exist.
committability.author_follow_up: Haibo Yan revived the patch in 2026 and posted v9 to fix the security check found in review. The entry has needed a rebase since 2026-11-05.

priority.reason: The goal is valid and costs fall only on range joins, but message #6 says such joins are rare and no committer has reviewed v5 to v9. Review cost is judged from the touched files; the code was not read.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the ASan crash from January 2024, the bounds handling in the merge walk and the coverage of the security check in every estimator path could not be judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve join selectivity estimation using extended statistics
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch uses per-table extended statistics, mainly functional dependencies, when it estimates join selectivity in clausesel.c. It also tries to combine join clauses with relation-level filters in calc_joinrel_size_estimate to estimate conditional probabilities.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra found the design at the wrong level of abstraction. Clausesel.c handled extended statistics directly, dependencies were applied clause by clause in a fixed order and only on the inner relation, and he proposed handling all join clauses for a pair of relations at once in extended_stats.c. The author agreed it could be done better but posted no new version. In July the patch no longer compiled, and it still did not one commitfest later, so it was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch includes some *very* interesting ideas, but I think it's does them too late and at the wrong level of abstraction.

precedents_retrieved.title: Using multicolumn statistics for more precise join selectivity estimatation
precedents_retrieved.objectors: vignesh C, Yugo NAGATA, Tomas Vondra
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch had two parts. One let the planner use extended (multicolumn) statistics, specifically functional dependencies, when estimating join selectivity. The other made auto_explain create multicolumn statistics automatically, or just suggest them, when a plan node's estimated row count differs from the actual count by more than a threshold.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The last visible message (July 2021) reports that the patch no longer compiled on Windows against changed ModifyTableState fields. The same message says Yugo Nagata's open review comments still needed addressing, and the entry was moved to Waiting on Author. Those comments included duplicate statistics suggestions causing a unique-constraint error, redundant suggestions, and a request to explain why each statistic is suggested. Earlier, Tomas Vondra had suggested moving the advisor into a separate extension rather than auto_explain, collecting data across many runs, and not creating statistics automatically. The visible messages show no new version after that, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Also Yugo Nagata's comments need to be addressed, I'm changing the
status to "Waiting for Author".

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Enable parallel SELECT for "INSERT INTO ... SELECT ..."."
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Enable parallel SELECT for "INSERT INTO ... SELECT ..."."
Reverted commit(s): Doc: Update description for parallel insert reloption.; Add a new GUC and a reloption to enable inserts in parallel-mode.; Improve FK trigger parallel-safety check added by 05c8482f7f.; Enable parallel SELECT for "INSERT INTO ... SELECT ...".; Fix use of relcache TriggerDesc field introduced by commit 05c8482f7f.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
To allow inserts in parallel-mode this feature has to ensure that all the
constraints, triggers, etc. are parallel-safe for the partition hierarchy
which is costly and we need to find a better way to do that. Additionally,
we could have used existing cached information in some cases like indexes,
domains, etc. to determine the parallel-safety.

List of commits reverted, in reverse chronological order:

ed62d3737c Doc: Update description for parallel insert reloption.
c8f78b6161 Add a new GUC and a reloption to enable inserts in parallel-mode.
c5be48f092 Improve FK trigger parallel-safety check added by 05c8482f7f.
e2cda3c20a Fix use of relcache TriggerDesc field introduced by commit 05c8482f7f.
e4e87a32cc Fix valgrind issue in commit 05c8482f7f.
05c8482f7f Enable parallel SELECT for "INSERT INTO ... SELECT ...".

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallel INSERT (INTO ... SELECT ...)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set allows parallel execution of both the INSERT and the SELECT parts of "INSERT INTO ... SELECT ...", with workers inserting tuples themselves; where parallel insert is unsafe (for example foreign keys or ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE), only the SELECT part is parallelised. It changes the planner, executor and parallel-worker code, adds parallel-safety checks on the target table (including partitions, triggers and domains), and adds a GUC and a reloption to control the feature.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Parts of the work, "Parallel SELECT for INSERT" and the related GUC/reloption, were committed during the thread. The remaining patches, which add the parallel INSERT functionality itself, were marked Returned with Feedback because of feedback given on pgsql-committers, which said a lot of work remained. The visible messages do not show the content of that feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There is a lot of work
to do for this patch as per the feedback given on pgsql-committers
[1].

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Use Foreign Key relationships to infer multi-column join selectivity".
precedents_retrieved.authors: Simon Riggs, Tom Lane, Robert Haas
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Use Foreign Key relationships to infer multi-column join selectivity".
Reverted commit(s): Use Foreign Key relationships to infer multi-column join selectivity; Load FK defs into relcache for use by planner; Clean up foreign-key caching code in planner.; Minimal fix for crash bug in quals_match_foreign_key.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts 137805f89 as well as the associated commits 015e88942,
5306df283, and 68d704edb.  We found multiple bugs in this feature, and
there was concern about possible planner slowdown (though to be fair,
exhibiting a very large slowdown proved difficult).  The way forward
requires a considerable rewrite, which may or may not be possible to
accomplish in time for beta2.  In my judgment reviewing the rewrite will
be easier to accomplish starting from a clean slate, so let's temporarily
revert what's there now.  This also leaves us in a safe state if it turns
out to be necessary to postpone the rewrite to the next development cycle.

precedents_retrieved.title: Relax requirement for INTO with SELECT in pl/pgsql
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a pl/pgsql SELECT, or a DML statement with RETURNING, run without INTO and discard its result instead of raising "query has no destination for result data". This would deprecate PERFORM and bring pl/pgsql closer to plain SQL.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The idea had broad support (+1 from Jim, Merlin, Robert, Tom, David J. and Brendan Jurd). Pavel Stehule's -1 rested on the SQL standard and Oracle, both of which require INTO, but he later called his opinion minor. David G. Johnston's review asked for reworked documentation and at least one new test. Merlin Moncure agreed to resubmit but sent no updated patch, so Peter Eisentraut returned it with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think we are waiting on an updated patch, with docs and tests.

precedents_retrieved.title: estimating joins using extended statistics
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch uses multi-column MCV lists from extended statistics to estimate equijoin selectivity, matching the MCV lists of the two joined relations the way eqjoinsel_inner does. It can also use base restrictions as conditions on the MCV lists, and estimates joins of more than two relations one relation pair at a time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer objected to the design in the visible messages. The last messages report that the 2022-01-01 version fails cfbot with uninitialized-variable warnings in mcv_combine_simple() and no longer applies to master, and no new version appears before the entry was returned. The author still listed open items, such as no support for outer or inequality joins and possibly wrong ndistinct and nullfract assumptions for column subsets.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Also the patch doesn't apply anymore:

precedents_retrieved.title: PoC: improving join estimates using sampling
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a "sample" kind to create statistics, so the planner samples tables during planning to estimate scan and join selectivity. Joins on a primary key use correlated sampling: the planner samples the table without the key randomly and looks up the matching rows in the other table.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Planning overhead was too high: the two-table example took about 600 ms to plan. The planner sampled the same relation several times, and the correlated sample ran one SPI lookup per row. Andres Freund noted the PoC had not been updated since January and was in the final CF, and he said the planner first needs a way to tell cheap plans from expensive ones so it samples only when useful. Tomas Vondra agreed it should be moved or returned, and that sampling would stay too expensive for simple queries.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But even if we manage to make this much cheaper, there will still be
simple queries where it's going to be prohibitively expensive.

precedents_retrieved.title: improving join estimates using FK
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the planner use foreign keys between joined tables to estimate join selectivity, so a multi-column join that matches a foreign key gets an estimate of about 1/N of the referenced table. Later versions also tried to find foreign keys through equivalence classes and to handle joins of more than two relations.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was closed because the author did not post a new version after David Rowley's revised patch, which was waiting for the author's review. Open design problems remained: with several relations on one side of the join, the same foreign key can match more than once, and taking the minimum selectivity was a known approximation. Also, the referenced rows may not all be present in a joined relation.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Tomas, I think we need you need to submit a new version of this patch, please.  Closing it for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab completion for SELECT in psql
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql tab completion after SELECT, suggesting column names from all visible tables and function names. Functions that are unlikely to be called directly are filtered out, and later versions use per-server-version queries and add completion after commas.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas found the completions both too broad and too narrow: system catalog columns flood short prefixes, the FROM clause is ignored, and system columns appear inconsistently. He held that the completion must be smarter to be acceptable. He also reported that the query on pg_attribute took about 1 second on a database with a 1000-partition table. An earlier review by Peter Eisentraut found broken older-version queries and an unsettled function filter. The rebased patch of 2018-09-22 got no visible reply before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think the completion needs to be smarter to be acceptable.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent proposes this idea; [P1], [P8], [P9] and [P6] cover other join estimation methods, and their reasons do not apply. Message #29 points to this patch's own earlier CommitFest entry, which stalled on the CFbot ASan abort (messages #16 to #18), a code question outside this angle.

The patch adds no syntax, keyword, GUC, psql command or dumpable object; it only changes oprjoin for built-in range and multirange operators. These changes reach users only through a major-version catalog update, and plan changes after upgrade are the expected effect of a better estimate. The && overestimate for sparse multiranges was settled in messages #23-#24. Not checked without the code: whether the oprjoin entries that are replaced are referenced anywhere outside these operators.

The proposal has no persistent or cross-node state beyond new built-in pg_proc entries and oprjoin settings in pg_operator.dat, which only need the usual catversion bump. It changes no on-disk format, WAL record, statistics layout, wire protocol or extension ABI, and the new rangetypes_selfuncs.h is backend-private.

The only privilege question is the missing statistic_proc_security_check() before support functions run over another role's bounds histogram (message #31). v9 adds the check for both sides of both estimators, falls back to the default selectivity, and adds privileges.sql tests (message #32). The merge walk is linear in histogram size, so it gives no new denial-of-service path. The January 2024 ASan out-of-bounds read (messages #16, #18) is a code-level question this angle cannot judge without the code.
Hot-path cost is limited to range and multirange join clauses, so non-users pay nothing. The multirange && approximation and the duplication concern were settled in messages #23-#25.

Postgres has no existing way to get these estimates. The range && operator uses a fixed default today, and rewriting r1 << r2 as upper(r1) < lower(r2) only reaches scalarltjoinsel, which is also a constant. No extension that does this is known to me, and estimators for built-in range operators belong next to the existing restriction estimators in rangetypes_selfuncs.c. Patch 3 removes duplicated helpers rather than adding a second mechanism.
Costs fall mostly on queries that use these operators, so this is a not now, show demand point and not grounds for rejection.
